newsitem.title: UK: LME base metals drift off in lustreless pre-market.
newsitem.headline: LME base metals drift off in lustreless pre-market.

text.p: Base metals prices drifted lower in inter-office trade on Tuesday following unsupportive London Metal Exchange (LME) stock data.
Three months copper crumbled steadily and was last indicated at $2,450/55, down from $2,474 at the previous kerb close, while cash/threes backwardation contracted somewhat to $55/$60 from around $70.
A stock drawdown of 475 tonnes failed to provide any buoyancy to the market, which some analysts said needed to consolidate after recent big gains.
Instead the market may come under pressure after prices twice failed to surmount stiff resistance at $2,490 over the last two trading days, traders said.
Stops were said to lurk around $2,420.
Aluminium was also lower, at $1,640/42, down from $1,653 at Monday's kerb close.
LME stocks notably rose by 2,050 tonnes, the first such rise since daily reporting started on April 7.
Traders had attributed some of the recent drawdowns to metal being taken off LME warrant and placed on consignment.
But aluminium's contango was becoming less attractive for consigning deals in recent days, which could have resulted in inventories rising on Tuesday, some traders said.
The market may come under pressure as players sniff out stops on the downside.
Some support is expected around $1,625/30 area.
Zinc was also $9 easier at $1,333 and traders said a correction towards $1,324 was not unexpected after Monday's weaker close.
Monday's massive LME stock rise of 12,200 tonnes was followed on Tuesday by a tiny 125-tonne decline.
Nickel, last at $7,720/40, was down sharply from Monday's $7,855 finish.
Prices had advanced well on Monday to above the $7,900 resistance level but the gains were shortlived, catching some market players off guard.
But a sizeable stocks decline of 1,260 tonnes pulled the rug out from under the market.
Technically, a gap between $7,660 and $7,620 may be filled, analysts said.
Lead, at $618/$620, was little changed from Monday's easier close. Tin was very quiet and steady at $5,730/50.
Alloy was last at $1,500, compared to $1,505/10.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
